native_driver_coverage.meaning: 0 accepts; 1 rejects with diagnostic; 2 declines without validity claim. Unscored coverage controls.

architecture.public_gap: One BFX format exists, but README exposes bounded and streaming source routes and manual optimizer staging. A single practical native compilation entry point is not yet implemented at this baseline.
architecture.format: BFX NUL magic, identifier01, fixed one-byte operations and u32 count; no live legacy decoder. Existing set has ASCII primitives, CLEAR, arithmetic/movement powers. Affine/scan/offset operations are not implemented.
architecture.ownership: BBC standard BF owns filtering, validation and semantic optimization. XAX canonical graphs own orchestration, import, verification, native lowering and packaging. External tools measure and invoke existing APIs only.
python_production_dependencies: process orchestration in current external development workflow
native_driver_limits: Native full BBC end-to-end host not integrated
General common Windows helper-loader still falls back to Python

limitations: The baseline is pinned to the canonical migration revision; historical reports are not relabeled.
Three selected workloads and exploratory run clusters do not support a general competitor victory.
Awib and fresh sustained-runtime/process-runtime/real-application scores are not measured in this baseline.
OS file caches are warm; no hardware cold-boot or thermal control.
Resident/commit counters are Windows kernel single-process lifetime peaks, not a sampled process-tree sum.
Stage timing is instrumentation: Android generic API combines lowering, verification and packaging; startup/store-read include lazy helper setup. No separate helper-only cost is invented.
The worker also saves a bound store snapshot inside the measured process, and records hashes/JSON. No harness overhead is subtracted.
Native build-driver controls are unscored acceptance/decline checks, not complete-build benchmarks.
